target.title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Age Estimation Using B-Mode Ultrasound Tongue Image

entries.text: The authors say no prior study had used ultrasound tongue images to predict speaker age.
entries.condition: Novelty claim in related work; based on the authors' knowledge at publication.

entries.text: The conclusion calls this the first attempt to predict age from ultrasound tongue images.
entries.condition: Authors' novelty claim; proof-of-concept study using UPX and UXTD child data.

entries.text: The abstract reports 2.03 as MAE for typically developing children.

questions.q: Are the headline values 2.03 and 4.87 MAE or MSE, and what evaluation split do they represent?
questions.answer: The abstract labels both as MAE, while the results section and tables describe them as validation MSE. The body uses a random 80/20 train-validation split and reports no independent test set, so the metric conflict remains unresolved.

questions.q: Do these results establish generalization to unseen speakers or sessions?
questions.answer: No such separation is reported. The paper randomly assigns data to train and validation and does not say whether speakers, sessions, or utterances are held out as groups.

questions.q: Which reproducibility conditions are missing from the paper?
questions.answer: The paper does not report random seeds or repeated runs, image normalization, explicit model-selection criteria, or a chance-level comparator; augmentation selection and headline validation results use UXTD validation data.

questions.q: For Ribeiro 2019, Diener 2020, Shandiz 2021 and Eshky 2019: the evaluation split (held-out speakers or sessions), the CNN accuracies for seen versus unseen speakers, the speaker-trait UAR and chance, and the single-frame speaker-recognition error.

questions.q: Triage #3: is there a third earlier held-out-speaker study on the UltraSuite child corpora?
questions.answer: Wiki UltraSuite papers before 2020-07: UltraSuite 2018 (dataset; speaker-labelling test set only), Ribeiro 2019 diarization (evaluation utterances, no held-out-speaker design stated), Ribeiro 2019 phonetic classification (LOSO, yes), Eshky 2019 synchronisation (held-out UXTD/UPX speakers, yes). Only two; Fabre 2015 is a different setting (tongue contour tracking, 9 speakers). M12 downgraded to standard.
